sources.ref_file_title: KZ22 - An Analysis of the Algebraic Group Model
sources.authors: Cong Zhang, Hong-Sheng Zhou, Jonathan Katz
sources.note: ePrint 2022/210 (author order there: Katz, Zhang, Zhou); ASIACRYPT 2022 proceedings order is Zhang, Zhou, Katz (cryptobib AC:ZhaZhoKat22, which the existing reference page already uses). Abstract verified via search snippet: 'as the GGM and AGM are currently formalized, this is not true: hardness in the AGM may not imply hardness in the GGM, and a generic reduction in the AGM may not imply a similar reduction in the GGM.' The existing reference page lists only Katz and Zhang; Zhou is missing. Keeping key KZ22 because the page exists.

sources.ref_file_title: JM24 - Generic and Algebraic Computation Models When AGM Proofs Transfer to the GGM
sources.note: cryptobib C:JaeMoh24; ePrint 2025/2121. Abstract verified via search snippet: KZZ22 'gave an interpretation of the claim under which it is incorrect'; JM24 'give an alternate interpretation under which it is correct, using natural frameworks for capturing generic and algebraic models for arbitrary algebraic structures. Most algebraic analyses in the literature can be captured by our frameworks.' Whether the framework is Maurer-style could not be confirmed; not asserted.

pages.class_justification: KZ22 refute the FKL18 transfer by counterexample under the formalizations of the GGM and AGM in use, which would be `free` by the repo's convention; but JM24 show the transfer holds under an alternative formalization covering most algebraic analyses in the literature, and the wiki's `ggm` node spans both Shoup's and Maurer's formulations. Neither endpoint is a primitive, and the claim's truth depends on which formalization is meant, so no class is recorded; the scoping lives in the statement.
pages.model_justification: Barrier frontmatter carries no model field. Both endpoints are idealized models, and the barrier is scoped to Shoup-style GGM vs AGM as KZ22 formalize them; that scoping is carried in the statement text.
pages.statement: As the two models are currently formalized, hardness in the [[algebraic-group-model|AGM]] does not imply hardness in the [[generic-group-model|GGM]], and a generic reduction in the AGM need not yield a corresponding reduction in the GGM — [[KZ22 - An Analysis of the Algebraic Group Model|KZ22]]. This refutes the transfer claimed by [[FKL18 - The Algebraic Group Model and its Applications|FKL18]] under that formalization; under the alternative formalization of generic and algebraic computation of [[JM24 - Generic and Algebraic Computation Models When AGM Proofs Transfer to the GGM|JM24]] the transfer holds for most algebraic analyses in the literature.
pages.improvements_text: - Under an alternative formalization of generic and algebraic computation, the FKL18 transfer claim is correct, and most AGM analyses in the literature fall within it — [[JM24 - Generic and Algebraic Computation Models When AGM Proofs Transfer to the GGM|JM24]]
notes_to_keep: `content/Glossary/generic-group-model.md` states the FKL18 direction without mentioning KZ22; the two glossary pages still disagree about what is settled.
Barriers between idealized *models* (rather than primitives or assumptions) are a hypothesis shape the hyperedge schema does not type; MPZ20's hierarchy of GGM variants is a second instance.

sources.ref_file_title: RT19 - Oracle Separation of BQP and PH
sources.note: cryptobib STOC:RazTal19 (STOC 2019, pp. 13-23, DOI 10.1145/3313276.3316315); ECCC TR18-107. Bibliographic data verified against cryptobib; the abstract itself could not be fetched (ECCC, ACM DL, Semantic Scholar blocked). Result: a distribution over {+-1}^{2N} distinguished from uniform by a one-query quantum algorithm with advantage Omega(1/log N) but not by quasi-polynomial-size constant-depth circuits, giving an oracle A with BQP^A not in PH^A.

pages.class_justification: An oracle separation rules out exactly the relativizing class: RT19 give an oracle relative to which BQP is not contained in PH, hence not in NP, so no relativizing proof can establish the inclusion. It says nothing about non-relativizing arguments, and per the partial order it also kills any fully-black-box argument.
pages.model_justification: Barrier frontmatter has no model field; the separation is relative to an oracle, which is recorded via `class: relativizing` and stated in the text.
pages.statement: There is an oracle relative to which $\classBQP \not\subseteq \mathbf{PH}$, hence one relative to which $\classBQP \not\subseteq \classNP$ — [[RT19 - Oracle Separation of BQP and PH|RT19]]. No relativizing argument places [[bounded-error-quantum-polynomial-time|BQP]] inside [[nondeterministic-polynomial-time|NP]]; unrelativized, neither containment between the two classes is known.
pages.sketch: Raz and Tal exhibit a distribution over $\{\pm 1\}^{2N}$, a variant of Forrelation, that a quantum algorithm making one query distinguishes from uniform with advantage $\Omega(1/\log N)$, while no constant-depth circuit of quasi-polynomial size distinguishes it with advantage better than $\polylog(N)/\sqrt{N}$; the standard diagonalization turns this black-box separation into the oracle.
flags: no-bqp-to-np: HIGH — the migrated Simon sentence should be dropped, not repaired. Simon's problem is a promise problem, and under the promise a single collision certifies the 2-to-1 case, so 'in BQP but not in NP relative to a random oracle' is not a correct statement of the separation. Raz-Tal is the clean citation. The same sentence still sits on content/Complexity/bounded-error-quantum-polynomial-time.md (Known relationships).

no-bqp-to-np: `strength: unconditional` reads as 'BQP is unconditionally not in NP', which is open. What is unconditional is the oracle separation; a human should confirm how `strength` is meant to interact with `class: relativizing`.

no-bqp-to-np: earlier oracle separations via Recursive Fourier Sampling (Bernstein-Vazirani) are frequently cited for BQP not in MA (hence not in NP) relative to an oracle. I could not verify from a primary source which paper proves the MA/NP form (only secondary statements in Aaronson's 'BQP and the Polynomial Hierarchy'), so only RT19 is proposed as the source.

no-bqp-to-np: RT19's abstract could not be fetched from any host; bibliographic data is confirmed by cryptobib and the sketch's parameters are from the verifier's knowledge of the abstract. Confirm the parameters when creating the reference page.
verifier_changes: statement: tightened wording; 'open in both directions' → 'neither containment is known'
sketch: 'the gap is the Forrelation problem' → 'a variant of Forrelation'; \mathrm{polylog} → \polylog macro; tightened
source note: recorded that only bibliographic data (cryptobib) could be verified independently

pages.class_justification: The separation is an explicit counterexample, not a restriction on proof technique: from any CPA-secure scheme, appending a constant bit to every ciphertext yields a scheme that is still CPA-secure and trivially distinguishable from uniform. That rules out the implication itself, which is `free` by the repo's convention for barriers.
pages.statement: [[symmetric-key-encryption#ind-cpa-security|IND\$-CPA security]] is strictly stronger than [[symmetric-key-encryption#cpa-security|CPA security]]: appending a constant bit to every ciphertext of a CPA-secure $\SKE$ preserves CPA security, while an IND\$-CPA adversary that checks the bit on one query has advantage $1/2$ — folklore.
pages.sketch: The appended bit is independent of the message, so a CPA adversary against the modified scheme yields one against the original; a uniform ciphertext carries the constant bit only with probability $1/2$.
flags: no-cpa-security-to-ind-cpa-security: the object page content/Primitives/symmetric-key-encryption.md:80 states 'IND$-CPA implies CPA security, but not vice versa' as one sentence. The forward half is a separate reduction edge (no ind-dollar-cpa-security => cpa-security page exists in content/Reductions/) and should be split out from this barrier.

no-cpa-security-to-ind-cpa-security: the counterexample is folklore, but the IND$-CPA notion itself is attributable (Rogaway's nonce-based / indistinguishability-from-random-bits formulations). If the SKE page ever cites the notion's origin, this barrier should link it rather than restate it.

statement/sketch: tightened wording; advantage 1/2 re-derived under the |2Pr-1| convention (Pr[b'=b] = 3/4)

pages.wrong_reason: The page records an uncited, double-hedged note ('I think this version of PIR might get around the DMO00 barrier'), not a result, and the `depir` node is ambiguous between variants on which the claim has different truth values. Unkeyed and public-key DEPIR are non-trivial single-server PIR schemes (the server can run Setup itself; query-time communication is o(n)), so DMO00 applies and those variants imply OT — the chain the wiki already records as content/Reductions/depir-to-cpir.md and content/Reductions/cpir-to-ot-dmo00.md, which this barrier contradicts. Only secret-key DEPIR plausibly evades DMO00, and for a different reason than the page gives: the client, not the server, runs Setup and sees the whole database, so no non-trivial single-server PIR protocol results. Even there the evasion is not a theorem. The supportable edge, if one is wanted, is a relativizing barrier on {secret-key PIR} => OT, argued from BM26 (SK-PIR from one-way functions, if that construction relativizes) composed with IR89 (no relativizing reduction from one-way permutations to key exchange) and OT => KE; both papers have reference pages.
flags: no-depir-to-ot-dmo00: HIGH — as recorded this barrier contradicts the wiki's own composition depir-to-cpir + cpir-to-ot-dmo00. Either delete the page or re-type it on the secret-key variant.

no-depir-to-ot-dmo00: the `depir` node is ambiguous between SK-, PK- and unkeyed DEPIR (content/Primitives/doubly-efficient-pir.md declares only an `unkeyed-depir` variant), and the claim's truth value differs across those variants. Typing any DEPIR barrier requires splitting the node first.

Fixing that sentence is a reference-fixer/editor lane item on the BIPW17 page.

pages.wrong_reason: The hyperedge is degenerate and the underlying results are not reduction barriers. Both endpoints resolve to the same object: content/Assumptions/learning-with-errors.md maps the variant keys `evasive-lwe-private-coin`, `private-coin-evasive-lwe`, `circular-evasive-lwe` and `evasive-lwe` all to the single anchor `#evasive-lwe`, so the page asserts that a reduction from X to X yields a contradiction. The page is also a near-duplicate of content/Barriers/no-evasive-lwe-to-evasive-lwe-buw24.md, which records the same passage under the sibling variant key.

pages.wrong_reason: No theorem states that KEA-like assumptions cannot be derived from falsifiable assumptions; the claim marked '— standard' on content/Assumptions/knowledge-of-exponent.md conflates two results. (i) Gentry–Wichs (STOC 2011; cryptobib STOC:GenWic11) rule out black-box reductions from any falsifiable assumption to the *adaptive soundness of a SNARG* — the sibling edge bar-falsifiable-assumption-to-snark-gro16, whose conclusion object is SNARK, not KEA. (ii) Bitansky–Canetti–Paneth–Rosen (STOC 2014; cryptobib STOC:BCPR14) show that if indistinguishability obfuscation exists then extractable one-way functions with unbounded auxiliary input do not, which *refutes* a class of knowledge assumptions rather than barring a reduction to them. That KEA is non-falsifiable describes the assumption's syntactic form, not a barrier, and 'a black-box reduction to KEA' is not even well-typed: a KEA violation is not witnessed by any efficient adversary the reduction could run as an oracle. As recorded the page duplicates the GW11 edge with the wrong conclusion object and should be deleted or re-typed onto SNARG adaptive soundness.

Disposition is wrong_claim rather than undetermined because the recorded sentence misstates both.

sources.ref_file_title: GW11 - Separating Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments From All Falsifiable Assumptions
sources.note: cryptobib STOC:GenWic11 (STOC 2011, pp. 99-108, DOI 10.1145/1993636.1993651); ePrint 2010/610. Abstract verified verbatim via the Microsoft Research mirror: 'black-box reductions cannot be used to prove the security of any SNARG construction based on any falsifiable cryptographic assumption ... extends to designated verifier SNARGs ... and slightly succinct SNARGs, whose size is only required to be sub-linear in the statement and witness size.' The 'sub-exponentially hard subset-membership problem' qualifier is from the paper's main theorem, not its abstract; the paper text could not be fetched (eprint, ACM DL blocked). WW24's abstract snippet independently reads GW11 as requiring sub-exponential hardness.

sources.ref_file_title: WW24 - Adaptively-Sound Succinct Arguments for NP from Indistinguishability Obfuscation
sources.note: cryptobib STOC:WatWu24 (STOC 2024, pp. 387-398, DOI 10.1145/3618260.3649671); ePrint 2024/165. Abstract verified via search snippet: first adaptively-sound SNARG for NP in the plain model from sub-exponentially-hard iO, sub-exponentially-hard one-way functions, and polynomial hardness of discrete log or factoring; the abstract reads GW11 as requiring 'sub-exponential hardness (and complexity leveraging)'.

pages.class_justification: GW11 exclude every reduction that uses the cheating prover only as an oracle, for arbitrary SNARG constructions; fully-black-box reductions are a subclass of these, while the classes that let the reduction depend on the adversary's code (semi-/weakly-black-box) are untouched. Recording `fully-black-box` fires the contradiction check on exactly the reductions GW11 rule out and on none they leave open.
pages.model_justification: Barrier frontmatter carries no model field. The barrier is a standard-model statement about SNARGs with a CRS; the AGM/GGM escape route lives on the companion reduction page content/Reductions/falsifiable-assumption-to-snark-gro16.md.
pages.statement: For any NP language with a sub-exponentially hard subset-membership problem, a black-box reduction from a [[falsifiable-assumptions|falsifiable assumption]] to the adaptive soundness of a [[succinct-argument|SNARG]] for that language in the CRS model exists only if the assumption is false. The separation covers designated-verifier SNARGs and slightly succinct ones, whose proofs need only be sublinear in the statement and witness length — [[GW11 - Separating Succinct Non-Interactive Arguments From All Falsifiable Assumptions|GW11]].
pages.sketch: Succinctness and the hardness of the language yield an unbounded cheating prover $P^*$ that outputs false statements with accepting proofs, whose statement–proof pairs are indistinguishable from those of an efficient prover $P$ that samples true statements with witnesses and proves them honestly (a leakage-simulation argument: the proof is a short function of the witness). A black-box reduction $R^{P^*}$ breaks the assumption; $R^{P}$ behaves indistinguishably, is efficient, and so breaks the assumption outright.
pages.improvements_text: - Adaptively sound SNARGs for NP nonetheless exist in the plain model, from sub-exponentially hard indistinguishability obfuscation and one-way functions together with the polynomial hardness of discrete log or factoring — [[WW24 - Adaptively-Sound Succinct Arguments for NP from Indistinguishability Obfuscation|WW24]]
flags: no-falsifiable-assumption-to-snark-gro16: HIGH — the frontmatter `source` must change from Gro16 to GW11. Gro16 is a construction paper and proves no barrier; it belongs only on the companion reduction page for the AGM escape route. The page slug carries the wrong paper suffix ('-gro16'); the file cannot be renamed cheaply (slugs are live URLs), so a human should decide whether to rename it to no-falsifiable-assumption-to-snark-gw11 or leave the slug as historical noise.

no-falsifiable-assumption-to-snark-gro16: the WW24 escape mechanism (complexity leveraging / super-polynomial reduction) is confirmed only by WW24's own abstract snippet, which says one reading of GW11 is that sub-exponential hardness and complexity leveraging are needed; the improvements bullet states only what WW24 achieves.

no-falsifiable-assumption-to-snark-gro16: consider also recording the tightness companion (Lipmaa-Pavlyk, 'Gentry-Wichs is Tight: a Falsifiable Non-adaptively Sound SNARG', ASIACRYPT 2021) — non-adaptive soundness *is* achievable from falsifiable assumptions. Not proposed as a source because later work reportedly disputes that construction; verify before citing.

no-falsifiable-assumption-to-snark-gro16: `strength: unconditional` — the theorem is conditional on the language having a sub-exponentially hard subset-membership problem; a human should decide whether `strength` should reflect that.

no-falsifiable-assumption-to-snark-gro16: sketch rewritten by the verifier — the researcher's version inverted the roles (it had the reduction's cheating prover replaced by an unbounded simulated prover); GW11's argument replaces the unbounded cheating prover by an efficient honest one. Mechanism recorded from the verifier's knowledge of the paper; the text could not be fetched.

sources.ref_file_title: GK03 - On the (In)security of the Fiat-Shamir Paradigm
sources.note: cryptobib FOCS:GolKal03 (FOCS 2003, pp. 102-115, DOI 10.1109/SFCS.2003.1238185); ePrint 2003/034. Bibliographic data verified against cryptobib; the paper could not be fetched (eprint, IEEE Xplore, Semantic Scholar blocked). The claim — a 3-round public-coin identification scheme secure in the ROM whose Fiat-Shamir signature scheme is existentially forgeable for every efficient hash function — matches the abstract on the existing reference page.

pages.class_justification: The result is a counterexample, not a restriction on proof technique: for the exhibited identification scheme the transformed signature is forgeable under *every* efficient hash function, so no argument of any kind establishes 'Fiat-Shamir plus a hash function yields a secure signature scheme'. Ruling out the implication itself is `free`.
pages.model_justification: Barrier frontmatter has no model field. The content of the result is precisely a model gap: the transform is secure in the random oracle model and fails in the standard model, which the statement says explicitly.
pages.statement: There is a 3-round public-coin identification scheme, secure in the [[random-oracle-model|random oracle model]], whose [[fiat-shamir-heuristic|Fiat-Shamir]] transform is an existentially forgeable [[digital-signature|signature scheme]] for every efficient [[hash-function|hash function]] instantiating the oracle — [[GK03 - On the (In)security of the Fiat-Shamir Paradigm|GK03]]. The random oracle in the transform is therefore not instantiable in general.
pages.sketch: The scheme adds an escape hatch: the prover may commit in its first message to a program and later prove, with a proof checkable in time independent of the program's running time, that the program maps the first message to the challenge. Interactively the challenge is chosen after the commitment, so the hatch is useless; after the transform the challenge is $H$ of the first message, and a forger commits to the code of $H$ itself.
notes_to_keep: The displayed inequality on content/Glossary/fiat-shamir-heuristic.md quantifies over $H$ but leaves $\calA$ and $\Pi$ unquantified; the theorem is 'there exists an identification scheme $\Pi$, secure in the ROM, such that for every efficient $H$ there is an efficient forger $\calA$'.

$\Pi_H$ is not defined on content/Glossary/fiat-shamir-heuristic.md ($\Pi_{\mathsf{FS}}$ is the notation introduced earlier), and the advantage superscript $\mathrm{uf}$ should use the $\ufcma$/$\eufcma$ macros.
flags: no-fiat-shamir-and-hash-function-to-ds-gk03: GK03's counterexample is constructed with Barak's non-black-box techniques, which rest on collision-resistant hashing, so the barrier is not literally assumption-free; `strength: unconditional` may need revisiting by a human.

no-fiat-shamir-and-hash-function-to-ds-gk03: the sketch is the standard account of GK03's construction (challenge-predicting committed program as an alternative accepting path) and could not be checked against the paper from this session; the verifier removed the attribution of the interactive scheme's soundness to Barak's techniques and the naming of the succinct-proof tool (CS proofs vs. universal arguments), which were unverified. Confirm against GK03 before publishing.

no-fiat-shamir-and-hash-function-to-ds-gk03: this barrier and no-fiat-shamir-to-nizk-gk03 are the same theorem read against two different conclusion objects (signatures, non-interactive arguments). Keeping both is defensible, but they should cross-link.

no-fiat-shamir-and-hash-function-to-ds-gk03: `class: free` records that the *universal* implication (every ROM-secure scheme, every hash function) is refuted. It does not contradict standard-model Fiat-Shamir for specific protocols via correlation-intractable hashing (e.g. CCH+19, PS19), which are different hyperedges; keep that in mind when those reductions are typed.

statement: tightened

sources.ref_file_title: GK03 - On the (In)security of the Fiat-Shamir Paradigm
sources.note: Same paper as the DS barrier; the object here is the non-interactive argument obtained by transforming a computationally sound interactive argument, not the signature scheme.

sources.ref_file_title: KRS25 - How to Prove False Statements Practical Attacks on Fiat-Shamir
sources.authors: Dmitry Khovratovich, Ron D. Rothblum, Lev Soukhanov
sources.note: cryptobib C:KhoRotSou25 (CRYPTO 2025, pp. 3-26, DOI 10.1007/978-3-032-01887-8_1); ePrint 2025/118. Removes the 'contrived protocol' caveat from GK03-style counterexamples. The existing reference page misnames the third author as 'Oleg Soukhanov'; cryptobib has Lev Soukhanov.

pages.class_justification: As in the signature case, the barrier is an explicit counterexample against every efficient hash instantiation, so it rules out the implication rather than a proof technique.
pages.model_justification: Barrier frontmatter has no model field; the statement is standard-model and says so. The positive direction (Fiat-Shamir for sigma protocols in the random oracle model) is a separate reduction edge with model: rom.
pages.statement: The [[fiat-shamir-heuristic|Fiat-Shamir]] transform of GK03's 3-round public-coin protocol, whose soundness is computational, is unsound for every efficient hash function, so the transform does not in general compile interactive arguments into sound [[non-interactive-zero-knowledge|non-interactive]] ones in the standard model — [[GK03 - On the (In)security of the Fiat-Shamir Paradigm|GK03]]. What fails is soundness, not zero knowledge, and the counterexample is an argument, not a proof.
pages.improvements_text: - GK03's counterexample is contrived by construction; Fiat-Shamir applied to the standard GKR-based succinct argument is also unsound, for explicit circuit families and every choice of hash function — [[KRS25 - How to Prove False Statements Practical Attacks on Fiat-Shamir|KRS25]]
flags: no-fiat-shamir-to-nizk-gk03: HIGH — the migrated bullet on content/Primitives/non-interactive-zero-knowledge.md says Fiat-Shamir 'is insecure for general interactive proofs'. GK03's counterexample is a computationally sound *argument*, not a proof; whether Fiat-Shamir is sound for interactive proofs is a separate, still-live question (see Bitansky et al., 'Why Fiat-Shamir for Proofs Lacks a Proof'). pages.class_justification: An explicit attack that works against every concrete hash instantiation refutes the implication itself, not a proof technique; `free` is the repo's value for that.
pages.model_justification: Barrier frontmatter has no model field. The result is a standard-model attack on a transform whose soundness holds in the random oracle model; the statement records that scoping.
pages.statement: Applying [[fiat-shamir-heuristic|Fiat-Shamir]] to the [[gkr-protocol|GKR]]-based succinct interactive argument for non-deterministic bounded-depth computation does not yield an adaptively sound [[succinct-argument|SNARK]] for any choice of hash function: there are explicit circuit families for which an efficient prover produces an accepting non-interactive proof of a false statement — [[KRS25 - How to Prove False Statements Practical Attacks on Fiat-Shamir|KRS25]]. The protocol is a standard, widely studied one, not a contrived counterexample.
